content:
AST SpaceMobile, Inc. (NASDAQ:ASTS) recovered some ground on Thursday, closing up about 2% at $60.45 after Wednesday's sector-wide decline.

The rebound came as satellite names stabilized following a Thursday statement from Rakuten Group confirming the first commercial service launch date for the partnership with AST SpaceMobile. Rakuten said service would begin in the first half of 2027.

The stock is still about 0.5% above its 20-day moving average of $60.15, but remains below the 50-day average of $62.89. Analysts note that the price must close above $65.50 to challenge the next resistance area. Support is still seen at $57.50.

ASTS shares are down about 19% over the past year, while Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ:SPCX) remains well ahead over the same period.
headline: AST SpaceMobile Rebounds Thursday After Rakuten Confirms 2027 Service Launch
summary: AST SpaceMobile rose about 2% to $60.45 after Rakuten confirmed a first half 2027 service launch, though it remains below its 50-day average.
